Avoid? Um... no, I wouldn't say I avoid things. Like, I don't call in sick to work or hide in bed, if that's what you mean. Actually, it's almost the exact opposite. I force myself to be right in the middle of everything, but I just agonize through every single second of it.

I'll sit there staring at the grid of webcams, over-analyzing everyone's facial expressions. If the lead developer mutes his mic or looks away when I start giving my update, my brain immediately goes, "He hates your proposal, he thinks your code is garbage, he's messaging the manager right now to complain about you." But I don't log off. I don't avoid the meeting. I just sit there and let the worry completely consume me while I try to keep talking normally. 

And it's the exact same way at home. I don't avoid my wife or the kids. I'll sit right there on the couch with them to watch a movie on a Friday night, right? But I'm not really *watching* the movie. I'm physically present—so I'm not avoiding family time—but mentally I'm a million miles away. I'll be staring at the screen but running through the mortgage rates in my head, or worrying if the rattling noise the refrigerator started making yesterday means we need to replace the whole unit, which is a huge expense we haven't budgeted for, and then I start worrying that my wife notices I'm distracted, which she usually does. 

So, I guess... I guess what I'm saying is, I show up to everything. I just can't enjoy any of it. I don't avoid situations, I just... I endure them. It's like I'm trapped in the situation and trapped in my own head at the exact same time. And I just keep pushing forward because, well, what else am I supposed to do? You can't just stop going to work or being a dad, you know? You just keep going, even when your brain won't give you a single second of peace. So, no, no avoidance. Just a lot of white-knuckling through the day.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Sadness? Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think so. It’s actually funny you ask that, because my wife asked me almost the exact same thing a couple of weeks ago. She came into the bedroom and saw me just sitting on the edge of the bed, staring at the wall, and she asked if I was getting depressed. But I had to try and explain to her that it’s... it's not sadness. I don't feel like crying, and I definitely don't feel hopeless, like I just want to give up or something.

I wouldn't care if David put me on a performance plan at work, or if the house literally fell apart around us, or if the kids didn't have enough saved for college. But I care *so* much. I care so intensely about every single little detail that it completely paralyzes me. When she saw me staring at the wall, I wasn't sitting there feeling sad—my brain was just running at a thousand miles an hour, trying to calculate every possible disastrous outcome for the week so I could somehow prevent them all. 

I *want* to do things. I want to finish fixing that guest bathroom sink. I want to be a great systems architect. I want to take my wife out to dinner and actually be present. I just get so terrified of making the wrong move or missing some crucial detail that I completely freeze up. So, no, I really wouldn't say I'm sad or down in the dumps. I'm just... I guess I'm just incredibly exhausted from being terrified all the time, if that makes sense? My engine is just constantly redlining, trying to keep all these plates spinning, and it's like I physically can't find the switch to turn it off. But no, definitely not sad. Just overwhelmed.

I'll be staring at the screen but running through the mortgage rates in my head, or worrying if the rattling noise the refrigerator started making yesterday means we need to replace the whole unit, which is a huge expense we haven't budgeted for, and then I start worrying that my wife notices I'm distracted, which she usually does. \n\nSo, I guess... I guess what I'm saying is, I show up to everything. I just can't enjoy any of it. I don't avoid situations, I just... I endure them. It's like I'm trapped in the situation and trapped in my own head at the exact same time. And I just keep pushing forward because, well, what else am I supposed to do? You can't just stop going to work or being a dad, you know? You just keep going, even when your brain won't give you a single second of peace. So, no, no avoidance. Just a lot of white-knuckling through the day.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any physical symptoms like tremors, sweating, or rapid heartbeat when you're worrying?\n\nPatient: Um, physical symptoms? Like, shaking or sweating? Honestly, no. I don't really get anything like that. It's funny you ask, because my wife actually asked me something similar the other day. She saw me just staring off into space while I was supposed to be helping with dinner—I was trying to chop some onions, but I was completely lost in this massive worry spiral about whether the kids' college funds were growing fast enough with inflation, which led to me worrying about the stock market, which led to me worrying about my own 401k—and she asked if I was feeling okay physically. Failing as an employee, failing as a husband, failing as a father to my kids. It's never just one topic. It's a complete, 360-degree worry about my entire existence, all day long.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel restless or on edge?\n\nPatient: Oh, yeah. Constantly. It’s actually funny, because when you asked about physical symptoms a minute ago, I was thinking about, like, my heart rate or breaking out in a cold sweat. But this... this is different. I just feel wound tight almost all day long. \n\nIt’s like my body is constantly bracing for something, you know? Like that split second before a car crash where you just tense every muscle and hold your breath? That’s me, all day. My shoulders are completely locked up. I have to consciously force them down, but five minutes later, they're locked right back up again. \n\nAnd sitting still? It feels completely impossible. I just can't do it.
